paper_of_the_week.title: Generalized Joint Laxity Is an Independent Predictor of Postoperative Resprain Following Anatomic Reconstruction Using Gracilis Tendon Autograft for Patients With Chronic Lateral Ankle Instability.
paper_of_the_week.clinical_summary: This cohort study addresses Ligament and return-to-sport rehabilitation. The reported population was: included in the GJL group (mean age at surgery, 27 The intervention or exposure was: anatomic reconstruction using gracilis tendon autograft from January 2018 to September 2023 with a minimum follow-up of 24 months were retrospectively evaluated and were divided in No clear between-group advantage was reported.
paper_of_the_week.practitioner_takeaway: This study may meaningfully inform practice in Ligament and return-to-sport rehabilitation. No clear between-group advantage was reported. Full-text review should still confirm the methods, intervention details, comparator, effect magnitude, adverse events, and applicability to the patient population.
paper_of_the_week.research_takeaway: Future studies should address the identified reporting and methodological limitations, particularly around effect estimates, precision, confounding, and clinical importance where applicable.
major_cautions: The retrospective design increases the risk of selection bias and incomplete data.
As an observational study, the findings may reflect confounding rather than causation.
Clinical importance or a minimally important difference is not clearly discussed.

specialist_takeaways.sports_performance: The study is relevant to Return to sport. Sports-performance confidence is high. Transfer to competitive athletes depends on training status, intervention specificity, outcome validity, and similarity to real competition demands.
specialist_takeaways.womens_athlete_health: This paper addresses female-athlete health. Women's-athlete-health confidence is high. Interpretation should consider whether female participants were adequately represented, whether sex-specific analyses were performed, and whether menstrual, hormonal, bone-health, and training variables were measured appropriately.
